sector_model: commercial-stage medical technology and transplant logistics service: judged on revenue growth, gross and operating margin trend, GAAP net income, cash flow after capital spending including aircraft finance leases, convertible and lease obligations, dilution, internal control status and regulatory dependence; capital intensity rose with aviation, so OCF alone overstates owner cash
thesis: TransMedics (Nasdaq: TMDX) sells the Organ Care System (OCS) for heart, lung and liver transplants and runs the National OCS Program with its own aviation logistics. Q3 2026 revenue 203.0M (+41%), 9M 566.9M vs 444.7M (+27%); FY2026 revenue guidance raised to 750-760M excluding PAD Aviation (764-774M including it, +26% to +28%). Q3 gross margin 58.5% (58.8%), Q3 income from operations 28.1M (+21%), net income 17.1M vs 24.3M; 9M operating income 65.2M vs 87.3M (-25%) and operating margin 11.5% vs 19.6% as operating expenses rose to 90.5M in Q3 from 61.3M on kidney, next-generation OCS and ENHANCE trial programs and the PAD Aviation consolidation (investment 2026-07-01). TTM net income 144.5M (FY2025 190.3M plus 9M 2026 39.1M minus 9M 2025 84.9M); TTM OCF 112.4M (192.8M plus 77.8M minus 158.3M) less TTM cash capex 67.7M (59.3M plus 52.1M minus 43.7M) gives TTM FCF about 44.7M before 340.0M of finance lease additions for aircraft (finance lease liability 351.5M at 2026-09-30). At the verified 2026-11-10 close of 90.96 and 34,733,883 shares (cover, 2026-11-02) market cap is about 3.16B: 21.9x TTM GAAP net income, FCF yield about 1.4%. Cash 493.0M; debt-like obligations 460.0M of 1.50% convertible notes due 2028 (conversion price about 94.00, close to the current price) plus the finance lease; enterprise value roughly 3.5B (own approximation). The stock rose 28% on 2026-11-06 (68.98 to 88.24) and a further 6.3% on 11-09 after the release and guidance raise. The market is paying for platform growth into new organs and Europe while current-year profit shrinks; the evidence in the filings shows growth but falling margins and rising capital intensity.
counterthesis: Profit is falling while revenue grows: 9M operating income -25%, diluted EPS Q3 0.46 vs 0.66 and 9M 1.08 vs 2.28, and investment spending (kidney, trials, headcount, headquarters, aviation) is rising faster than revenue. Cash conversion is weak: TTM FCF about 44.7M is about 1.4% of market cap, and the cash flow statement excludes 340.0M of aircraft acquired through finance leases, so true capital intensity is higher. The company reports a material weakness over inventory movement within its manufacturing network; disclosure controls were not effective at 2026-09-30 and remediation testing is expected to finish in Q4. Receivables rose 28.1M in 9M. Customer concentration, FAA and aviation regulation, and the CMS final rule on organ procurement organizations (released 2026-10-30; effect not read) are named risks, as is a securities class action. The 460M convertible matures June 2028 with a conversion price about 94, so dilution begins near the current price; interest expense rose (non-cash interest 13.9M in 9M). A 28% two-day jump on a modest guidance raise leaves less margin of safety. Kidney is first-in-human only in 2H 2027.
invalidation: Revenue growth falling below about 20% or guidance cut; Q4 or 2027 operating margin not recovering above the 2025 level of about 17.8% (FY2025 operating income not derived here; 9M 2025 was 19.6%); the material weakness leading to a restatement or an adverse audit opinion; an adverse CMS rule effect on organ procurement volume or OCS use; FAA or aircraft safety events; negative free cash flow after aircraft leases while leverage rises.
